plan.english: It dawned. Then the man stood up and put on footwear. Then he took gifts. His mother was cooking. Then he harnessed the two swift horses. Then his wife said to him, "Go, and return unharmed." Then his father said, "May the gods guard you!" Then he went out of the home, and the dog followed him. The sun came forth. The wheel of the sun was high. A bird was going ahead. Then he saw the long path. The path was long, and he did not become afraid. He was seeking great fame.

The way was long, and the hills were high. It was winter. Then the man was climbing the height. Snow lay on the hills. It became cold. His breath came forth, and he became tired. Then he saw a wolf. The beast was standing in the snow and kept looking at him. Then the man threw a stone, and the wolf fled. Then he sat down and ate, and leaned against the stone. It became warm, and the snow melted. Then he saw the distant river. Then he went down.

It was getting dark. Then the man sat down on the earth, and his two heels became tired. Then he prepared a fire. The fire was burning. It became cold. Then many stars shone. The night was long, and the darkness was thick. He was looking at the stars. "Stars, do you see my home?" The stars did not speak. "I remember my home." "Mother Earth, protect me!" The fire became slack. Then sleep seized him. Then it dawned, and the wheel of the sun came forth. Then he woke up and stood up.

A stranger came by the path. The man saw him and stood up. The stranger said, "Where are you going?" The man said, "I am going home. My home is far. Who are you?" "I am a stranger." "What is your name?" "My name is famous." "I do not know it." Then the two sat down together. The stranger gave him water, and they ate. Then the stranger said, "May the gods lead you!" And he went away. The man went forward.

It was getting dark. Then a guest came to the home. The father saw him and became joyful. He said, "Guest, sit down! Eat and drink!" Then the wife gave him water and butter. The fire was burning. The guest ate, and drank, and was sated. Then he spoke: "May the gods give good things to this home!" Then he lay down in the shelter. A guest is dear to the gods.

It was getting dark. The shepherd was leading the sheep to the hill. Then the dog heard the wolves and cried out. Three beasts were creeping. The shepherd saw them. The sheep trembled with fear. Then he said, "Fire, protect the sheep and me!" Then the fire became bright. The light of the fire was broad. The wolves saw the fire and fled. Then the sheep lay down. He was awake. Then it dawned. The sheep were alive. Fire is dear to him.

The stranger and the horse were going along the way. The sun was heating the two. They were thirsty, and they were sweating. They were seeking water, and they did not find it. Then the horse went forward, and the stranger followed it. They came to water. It was broad. Then the horse drank, and the stranger was drinking the water. Then the stranger sat down. Then they were satisfied. Whoever is thirsty, to him water is dear.

The driver was driving the wagon, and the two swift horses were pulling it. Then the wheel broke. The horses were standing still. The driver sat down and said, "Who will build a wheel?" Then a carpenter came. He saw the split wheel. He said, "I shall build a wheel. Give me a wage!" The driver gave him a wage. The carpenter was working, and he built the wheel, and smeared it with grease. Then he set the yoke in order. Then the driver drove the wagon again. The work of the carpenter is good.

title: The King's Son and the Serpent

plan.english: The son of the king, with swift horses, went by the long path. He drove the horses forward. Then he saw a serpent, which lay yonder. The serpent was great, and the earth was trembling. The serpent was devouring cattle. The horses trembled. Then he did not become afraid. "Serpent, you shut in the waters! Now I shall slay you." Then he slew the serpent, and the water became free. Then he set a famous name, and won imperishable fame. And he returned unharmed. A man dies; fame does not die.

The stranger saw a sitting shepherd on the hill. He said to him, "Where is the water?" The shepherd said, "It is yonder." And he pointed out the path. "Go down, and cross the field. Then you will see it." The stranger said, "Is the way long?" "The way is not long. May the gods protect you." Then the stranger went down.

title: Brother and Sister at the River

plan.english: The river was broad and swift. Then a brother and a sister came to it, and they were driving ten cattle. Then the sister spoke: "Let us cross!" Then the brother said, "It is swift. Do not go into the water!" And he trembled. Then the sister said, "I am not afraid." She drove them into the water. The cattle were swimming. They crossed it, and the brother and sister crossed after. Then they stood on the other side. The cattle drank water.

It rained. The rain-clouds were covering the sky. Then Perkʷunos gave thunder. Then the river became full, and the water was swelling. Then a stranger came to the water. He saw the great water. Then he said, "I shall not cross. I shall build a shelter." Then he lay down in the shelter and ate. The thunder went away, and the rain-clouds went away. Then it dawned, and the water was not great. The sun became bright. Then he crossed it.

A father and his son came to the water. The father said, "River goddess, you are swift! We give you a poured gift." Then he put the gift into the water. "Let us cross. Do not kill us!" The son trembled. It listened to them. Then the two crossed, and the water did not seize them. Then they stood on the other side. The father said, "The river goddess is unfailing."

A great boat was on the sea. Seven men were sitting in the boat. The leader drove the boat on. The boat carried them. They went three nights, and they became tired. The sun was heating them. The leader kept looking at a star, and the boat followed the star. Fish were swimming in the sea. It dawned. Then a bird came. The leader pointed out the bird. They became joyful.

The boat was going on the sea. Then the rain-clouds covered the sky, and the darkness became thick. Then Perkʷunos gave thunder. The sea became agitated, and the water was swelling. Then the men became afraid. The rope broke. The boat was splitting. Then the leader cried out, "Perkʷunos, rescue us!" Then they threw the silver into the sea. Then the thunder went away, and the rain-clouds went away. It dawned. They were alive.

title: The King's Son in the Sea

plan.english: The boat sank in the sea, and many dear ones died. The king's son was swimming in the water for three nights. It became cold. His heart did not tremble. He was looking at the stars. The stars were appearing. "Father Sky, rescue me!" Sky heard him. It dawned. Then he arrived at the earth. He seized it with his hands. Then he took great fame. The sea seized the boat; it did not seize his fame.

It dawned. The leader saw the earth. He cried out. They became joyful. Then the boat reached it. The men went out of the boat. They stood on it. They gave a gift to the sea. Then they prepared a fire. The fire was burning. They ate and drank. Then they lay down. "Mother Earth, you are dear!"

Two men came to the river. A boat-man was sitting there. Then they said, "Boat-man, carry us to the other side!" Then he said, "What will you give me?" "We shall give silver." "Sit down in the boat!" Then they gave it, and sat down in the boat. "Do not be afraid!" The boat-man drove the boat. The water was broad. Then the boat-man drove the boat forward. Then they stood on the other side. They said, "May the gods give you good things!"

There was darkness on the sea, and many stars shone. The boat was going. The leader kept looking at a star. Those stars were going around; that star stood. He said, "Star, lead us! We are confident." The boat followed the star. Then the sky was red. Then Dawn came, and the star went away. The sea became bright.

The sea is great. The rivers go to the sea. The sea is not filled. Fish live in the sea. Beasts do not live in the sea. No one ploughs the sea. There is no path on the sea. The boat is a path. The star points out the path to the boat. The sun sinks in the sea. Dawn, the daughter of Sky, becomes bright. The sea is dear to the fish. The sea gives men fish and death. Great is the sea.

The master was sitting at home. A trader came to him. He saw the two horses. He said, "Are these two horses young?" "They are young." "What is the price of the horses?" "The price is ten cattle." "High is the price! I shall give five cattle." "Give nine cattle!" "I shall give seven cattle." "Let that be!" Then the two made a pledge. The trader gave them, and took the two horses. The master drove them away. Then the trader harnessed the two horses. The two became joyful.

A woman carrying washed wool came to the trader. He saw her. He said, "Is the wool good?" She said, "It is good. I shall sell it." "Give it to me! I shall give you silver." Then she gave it to him, and he gave her silver, and she took it. Then the two became joyful. Then the trader bought much wool and carried it away. He sold it and took much silver. The trader became rich.

A trader put grease into the butter. Then he sold the butter to a young man. The young man ate the butter, and it did not become tasty. Then the young man seized him. "You deceived me!" "I did not deceive you!" Then the young man led him to the king. The king was sitting. The king heard the two. The king ate the butter, and it did not become tasty. Then he said, "You deceived! Give back the silver, and give a gift to the young man." Then the trader gave it back, and gave a gift. No one bought from him.

title: The Wolf and the Dog in Wool

plan.english: A wolf came to a shepherd. "Sell me a sheep!" "I shall sell you one." Then he clothed the dog in wool. The wolf gave a wild bull and took the dog. He did not recognize the dog. Then the wolf, carrying the dog, was going to the hill, and he became joyful. Then the dog seized the wolf and was tearing him. He cried out and fled. The shepherd drove the bull to the home. Whoever deceives is deceived.

The shepherd was sitting at the enclosure. A man came to him. He said, "I give you four cattle. Give me ten sheep!" The shepherd said, "The sheep are many. Let us make a pledge. Whoever breaks the pledge, may the gods slay him!" Then the shepherd got four cattle by trade, and the man got ten sheep by trade. The man drove the sheep away. The shepherd drove them into the enclosure. The two became joyful.

The trader harnessed the horses. Then he put the wool into the wagon. Then he went by the long path. He crossed rivers and hills. Then he arrived at the distant earth. There he was a stranger. In winter he dwelt there. He sold the wool and bought silver, a woman's garment and a horse. Then he put the garment into the wagon. Then he returned unharmed. He gave the garment to his wife. His name became famous.

A stranger who was buying came to the master of the wool. He said, "Your wool is not good!" The master said, "It is good. Look at it!" "It is not good. It is not good! I shall go away." "Do not go away! I shall give it to you." "What is the price?" "The price is not high." Then he gave silver and took it. Then he went away. Then he came again, and bought more wool.

The trader and the master made a pledge. Then the master gave five horses. Then the trader took the horses. He did not give the silver. "Where is the silver?" "The horses are not swift!" Then the master said, "Whoever breaks the pledge, Father Sky, strike him!" Then thunder came forth. And the home of the trader burned. Then he became afraid. He gave it to the master. The pledge stood.

For ten years the man of good fame was far from home. Then he came and sat down. The wife saw a stranger and gave him water. The dog was lying there. The dog knew him, and ran to him, and was licking his hands. The wife did not know him. Then the wife said, "Who are you?" He said, "I am your husband. My name is famous." Then her tears came forth, and she seized his hands. Whoever returns unharmed, to him the home is dear.

The mother was sitting at home. A young man came by the path. She did not recognize him. He was standing, and he cried out, "Mother!" She heard the word. Her heart knew the word. "Are you my son?" "I am your son." Then her tears came forth. Her two hands were trembling. She said, "Dawn has come to my home!" Then she ran, and seized him with her hands. The father heard it and went out.

The sister was ploughing in the field. A man was walking along the path. She did not look at him. Then the sister heard his step, and she knew it. Her heart trembled. She cried out, "Brother!" Then the sister, leaving the field, ran. The brother said, "Sister, I returned unharmed." She said, "Dear are you!" Then the two went home.

For ten years the king of good fame did not see the home. Then he came, and he was a stranger. The wife saw him, and she did not recognize him. She gave him water, and he drank it. He said, "I have seen the king." "Where have you seen him?" "I have seen him on the sea. He is alive." "He is alive?" "He will return unharmed." "May the gods lead him!" Then he said, "I am the king. My name is famous." The wife looked at him, and her heart knew him. Then her tears came forth.

A man went away and did not return. Then his mother cried out, "He died!" and his brother trembled. Seven years went. Then the stranger came to the home. The mother saw him and was afraid, and trembled. "You are dead! Do not come to my home!" He sat down and ate. Then he drank. The mother said, "The dead do not eat. You are alive!" Then she became joyful.

The wife kept looking at the path. In the night she saw the stars. She said to her heart, "Is he alive?" It said, "He is alive." Ten years went. She did not die. Then it dawned, and the sun came forth, and a man came by the path. The dog ran to him. Her heart knew him. "My heart did not deceive me."

title: Prayer to Father Sky for the Path

plan.english: Father Sky, guard my path! Make my way straight! God, show me the way! May the beast and the thief not seize me. May my two horses be swift. May the wheel of the sun be bright above. Now may my heart not tremble. May I not be thirsty, and may I return unharmed. Father Sky, giver of good things, hear me!

title: Prayer to Dawn Before the Journey

plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, come to me! You who drive the stars away; you who lead the wheel of the sun; you who are red; be bright on my path! Dawn, be bright on my horses! Dawn, bring light to me! Dawn, may my heart become joyful. Dawn, lead me to my home. Dawn, may I see your light.

Gods, protect my husband! May the beast and the thief not seize him. May the river be passable for him. May his horses be swift. Gods, may strength be his. May Perkʷunos not strike him. Make his path straight! May he return home unharmed. If he returns unharmed, I shall give you a gift.

Wolf and thief, flee! I am not afraid! Do not come near my horses! Now fire is around us. Perkʷunos is above. The earth, indeed, is below. Then fire singes the two. May Perkʷunos strike the teeth of the wolf! Go away, off from my path!
River, make your water stand! Do not seize me! May the water not be high; may it be passable! Now I shall cross, and I shall stand on the other side. May my horses cross; I shall give you a gift.

Mother Earth, I shall lie down. Mother Earth, guard me in the night. Now, stars, look at me! May the beast not eat me up; may sleep take me. May my horses lie beside me. May the night cover me; may the fire be burning. Dawn, may I wake in your light.
